content: Thrombophilias are conditions that predispose individuals to thrombotic events, and they have been linked to adverse pregnancy outcomes. These outcomes include intrauterine growth restriction, stillbirth, severe early-onset pre-eclampsia, and placental abruption. The administration of heparin during pregnancy has been proposed as a potential intervention to reduce the risk of these complications. The purpose of this review was to evaluate the effects of heparin on pregnancy outcomes in women diagnosed with thrombophilia. To achieve this, a comprehensive search was conducted across multiple databases, including the Cochrane Pregnancy and Childbirth Group's Trials Register, MEDLINE, EMBASE, CINAHL, and Scidex, as of July 2002. The search was later updated on August 3, 2012, and the results were added to a section awaiting classification. The review aimed to include randomized controlled trials that compared heparin with either a placebo or no treatment, as well as trials comparing different treatment regimens. Quasi-randomized studies were also considered eligible for inclusion. Data from the identified studies were to be extracted and recorded by two independent reviewers. However, no studies met the inclusion criteria for this review. As a result, there is currently no evidence from completed trials to determine the effects of heparin on pregnancy outcomes in women with thrombophilia. It is important to note that 23 citations remain in the awaiting classification section of the review. These citations may influence the conclusions of the review once they are assessed.
